Optimal Binning for Categorical Variables using Order-Restricted Bayesian Evidence

Source: R/obc_orbe.R
ob_categorical_orbe.Rd

Groups the categories of a feature so that the grouping and the number of groups maximize a Bayesian score of a constant event rate per group. A category keeps a group of its own only when the data support it. Reports posterior-mean WoE with credible intervals.

Usage

ob_categorical_orbe(
  feature,
  target,
  min_bins = 2,
  max_bins = 10,
  bin_cutoff = 0.05,
  max_n_prebins = 200,
  bin_separator = "%;%",
  prior_strength = 1,
  credible_level = 0.95,
  bin_penalty = 0,
  criterion = "predictive"
)

Arguments

feature

A character vector or factor of categories. Missing values form the category "NA".

target

A binary vector (0/1 or logical) with the same length as feature. Missing values are an error.

min_bins

Minimum number of bins (default: 2). It is honored whenever a grouping with that many bins satisfies bin_cutoff and has strictly increasing WoE; otherwise the largest feasible number of bins is returned. With min_bins = 1 a single bin is returned when the score does not support any split.

max_bins

Maximum number of bins (default: 10). The number of bins is selected by the score between min_bins and max_bins.

bin_cutoff

Minimum fraction of the rows in a bin, in \([0, 1)\) (default: 0.05). It is a constraint of the optimization. With bin_cutoff = 0 rare categories are merged only by the score.

max_n_prebins

Maximum number of atoms, the candidate units the bins are built from (default: 200). A feature with at most this many categories is searched over every boundary between categories in the order of their event rates. Above it, categories adjacent in that order are grouped into atoms of about equal frequency. Values above 1000 are treated as 1000, and the limit is lowered further when max_bins is large, to bound memory.

bin_separator

String placed between the categories of a merged bin in its label (default: "%;%"). A warning is issued when it occurs inside a category name.

prior_strength

Weight of the prior, in pseudo-events of the minority class (default: 1). Larger values shrink rare categories more strongly toward the overall event rate.

credible_level

Probability content of the WoE credible intervals, in \((0, 1)\) (default: 0.95).

bin_penalty

Cost of each bin beyond the first, in units of the log score, at most 1e6 (default: 0). Positive values give fewer bins and guard against splitting a feature unrelated to the target.

criterion

Score of a bin: "predictive" (default), the leave-one-out log predictive probability of its rows, or "evidence", its log marginal likelihood. "predictive" favors out-of-sample accuracy and returns more bins; "evidence" is more parsimonious. See Details.

Value

A list with one element per bin in the vectors below, in increasing order of WoE:

id

Bin identifiers (1-based).

bin

Bin labels: the categories joined by bin_separator.

woe

Posterior-mean Weight of Evidence.

iv

Information Value contribution, \((p_i - q_i) \, \mathrm{WoE}_i\), with \(p_i\) and \(q_i\) the observed shares of events and non-events.

count, count_pos, count_neg

Rows, events and non-events.

event_rate

Observed event rate.

woe_se

Posterior standard deviation of the WoE.

woe_lower, woe_upper

Limits of the equal-tailed credible interval of the WoE.

and the following:

total_iv

Sum of iv.

total_iv_corrected

total_iv minus the first-order sampling bias of a plug-in IV, floored at zero.

log_score

Score of the selected grouping.

log_score_by_bins

Score of the best grouping with \(1, 2, \ldots\) bins; NA where no grouping is feasible.

criterion

The criterion used.

order_probability

Posterior probability that the event rates of the bins are in the reported order.

converged

Always TRUE.

iterations

Number of bin counts evaluated.

Details

Model. The event rates of the groups are independent \(\mathrm{Beta}(a, b)\) with mean equal to the overall event rate \(\pi_0\) and \(\min(a, b)\) equal to prior_strength. For a group with \(n_i\) rows and \(e_i\) events, write \(A_i = a + e_i\) and \(B_i = b + n_i - e_i\).

Criterion. A grouping is scored by \(\sum_i f(n_i, e_i)\) minus bin_penalty for each group beyond the first. With criterion = "predictive", \(f\) is the leave-one-out log predictive probability of the rows of the group, $$f(n_i, e_i) = e_i \log\frac{A_i - 1}{A_i + B_i - 1} + (n_i - e_i) \log\frac{B_i - 1}{A_i + B_i - 1} ,$$ and with criterion = "evidence" it is the log marginal likelihood $$f(n_i, e_i) = \log \frac{B(A_i, B_i)}{B(a, b)} .$$ Both scores fall when a group is split into groups with equal observed event rates: by about one unit for the predictive score, and by an amount that grows as \(\frac{1}{2}\log n_i\) for the evidence, which therefore returns fewer groups in large samples. The grouping is chosen among many candidates, so with bin_penalty = 0 a feature unrelated to the target can still be split. A positive bin_penalty controls this: it multiplies the prior weight of a grouping by \(e^{-\mathrm{penalty}}\) for each additional group.

Search. Categories are ordered by their posterior-mean event rate \((a + e)/(a + b + n)\), which shrinks rare categories toward \(\pi_0\) before they are ordered. Ties are broken by count and then by name, so the result does not depend on the row order. The engine then finds, by dynamic programming, the grouping into bins contiguous in that order that maximizes the score, subject to bin_cutoff, the limits on the number of bins and strictly increasing posterior WoE. The search is exact among groupings contiguous in that order; groupings that are not contiguous are not examined.

Rare categories. Merging two groups changes the score by \(f(n_g + n_h, e_g + e_h) - f(n_g, e_g) - f(n_h, e_h)\). A category with few rows rarely carries enough information for a group of its own, so with bin_cutoff = 0 it is merged by the score, not by a frequency threshold.

WoE. As in ob_numerical_orbe, $$\mathrm{WoE}_i = \psi(A_i) - \psi(B_i) - \log\frac{\pi_0}{1 - \pi_0},$$ with posterior variance \(\psi'(A_i) + \psi'(B_i)\). The credible intervals are conditional on the selected bins.

References

Boullé, M. (2005). A Bayes optimal approach for partitioning the values of categorical attributes. Journal of Machine Learning Research, 6, 1431-1452.

Geisser, S., & Eddy, W. F. (1979). A predictive approach to model selection. Journal of the American Statistical Association, 74(365), 153-160.

See also

ob_numerical_orbe for numerical features and ob_categorical_dp for dynamic programming on the Information Value.

Examples

set.seed(123)
levels <- c(paste0("region_", 1:8), "rare_a", "rare_b")
prob <- c(rep(0.1, 8), 0.01, 0.01)
feature <- sample(levels, 3000, replace = TRUE, prob = prob)
rate <- c(0.05, 0.06, 0.10, 0.11, 0.20, 0.21, 0.35, 0.36, 0.15, 0.15)
target <- rbinom(3000, 1, rate[match(feature, levels)])

# bin_cutoff = 0 leaves the fate of the rare categories to the score
fit <- ob_categorical_orbe(feature, target, bin_cutoff = 0)

data.frame(
  bin = fit$bin, count = fit$count,
  woe = round(fit$woe, 3),
  lower = round(fit$woe_lower, 3),
  upper = round(fit$woe_upper, 3)
)
#>                            bin count    woe  lower  upper
#> 1          region_1%;%region_2   738 -1.095 -1.389 -0.818
#> 2          region_3%;%region_4   713 -0.809 -1.073 -0.558
#> 3 rare_a%;%region_6%;%region_5   771  0.040 -0.143  0.219
#> 4 rare_b%;%region_8%;%region_7   778  0.946  0.800  1.092
